chunks: And it is narrated from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) [that he] said:

A man will rise up from Qazwin, whose name will be the same as the name of a Prophet. People will make haste in accepting his authority; the disbeliever and the believer alike. He will fill the mountains with fear.
ai.seo_question: Who is the man from Qazwin mentioned in Shia eschatology?
ai.summary: In Shia eschatology, this hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi identifies the Dajjal (or a major false messiah figure) emerging from Qazwin, whose name matches a Prophet to facilitate widespread acceptance. His dominion is characterized by universal submission, where both polytheists and believers alike are compelled by his overwhelming presence, which is described as filling the mountains with fear. This event serves as a critical precursor to the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.s.), marking a period of global tribulation and spiritual testing.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 438 - It is narrated from the Messenger of Allah (s) that he said: “

A man will rise up from Qazwin, whose name will be same as the name of a Prophet. People will make haste in accepting his authority; but the mountains will be full of disbelievers and believers due to his fear.”
